Sam (People Ops): Heads up: launching a 6‑month pilot for PTO Carryover -> "Wellness Credit" conversion. You can convert up to 5 unused PTO days per calendar year into credits redeemable for caregiving, training, sabbatical-topup, or to donate to a teammate's leave. Pilot goes live May 1. Sign-up window May 1–31. Full doc: https://redwood.company/policies/wellness-credit-pilot :sparkles:
PeopleOps Bot: Event created: "Wellness Credit info session" Tue May 3 10:00–10:30 — calendar invite sent to all. :calendar:
Maya Chen: Quick q — is it 5 days per person per year or per employment period? Do I need manager approval?
Sam (People Ops): Good Q. It's up to 5 days per person per calendar year. No manager approval required for conversion — People Ops will process requests after the sign-up window closes. Approvals only needed if using credits to fund a paid sabbatical beyond existing policy.
Alex Rivera: Are these credits considered taxable? Can they be used for conference travel or purely caregiving/training?
Sam (People Ops): Credits are treated as a taxable benefit in some jurisdictions — we'll list region specifics in the doc and gross-up where appropriate. Primary uses are caregiving, professional development (course/conference fees), sabbatical top-ups, or donation to a colleague's leave fund. They can't be redeemed for standard personal travel reimbursements or cash payouts.
Jordan Patel: What happens to unused credits after the year? Roll over?
Sam (People Ops): For the pilot, unused credits expire at the end of the following calendar year. We plan to review after the pilot and adjust. Carryover cap for regular PTO remains unchanged (10 days) — this is an optional conversion on top of that.
Maya Chen: Thanks — where's the form to sign up?
Sam (People Ops): Form link in the policy doc above + pinned in #people-ops. We'll also drop a short explainer in #general tomorrow. :megaphone:
PeopleOps Bot: Reminder set — sign-up window closes May 31 23:59 PT. :alarm_clock:
